title: The category of groups exists, with morphisms bundled as a subtype
statement: CatS.grp is a CatS.CategoryLarge whose objects are AlgS.Group and whose hom-family is CatS.GrpHom G H := Subtype (G.carrier -> H.carrier) (CatS.IsGrpHom G H) -- a function TOGETHER WITH the proof that it respects both equivalences and carries G.op to H.op. Bundling is what makes the category's single congruence field provable: from g ~ g' and f ~ f' pointwise, K.equiv (g (f a)) (g' (f' a)) needs g to respect H.equiv, which an arbitrary function does not carry and a bundled morphism does. The unit and associativity laws are then reflexivity of the object's own equiv, because Subtype.val (Subtype.mk f h) iota-reduces, so both sides of each law are the same function.

evidence.supports: CatS.grp, CatS.GrpHom, CatS.mon, CatS.MonHom, CatS.IsMonHom, CatS.isMonHom_id, CatS.isMonHom_comp, CatS.isMonHom_congr, CatS.isGrpHom_congr and the record CatS.FunctorLarge all admit through the trusted Kernel::add_declaration gate with an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint. Two def_eq readings pin the content in BOTH directions: CatS.grp's hom-family IS the Subtype and is NOT the bare function space (which is the hom-family ADR-1620 measured as making compCongr false), and CatS.IsMonHom unfolds to congr AND (op AND unit) and NOT to congr AND op (which would be a semigroup morphism). Rejection controls with unmutated positive twins in the same test: N1 a compCongr whose conclusion names comp v u' instead of comp v' u' is refused; N2 the wrongly ordered composite of two monoid homomorphisms is refused.

The two tests that carry this fact are groups_tests::the_group_category_has_bundled_morphisms and groups_tests::a_monoid_morphism_preserves_the_unit; the two mutations are groups_tests::n1_the_congruence_concludes_about_both_replaced_morphisms and groups_tests::n2_the_composite_monoid_hom_is_ordered.

notes: Subtype and not Sigma, and the levels decide it rather than taste: CatS.CategoryLarge's hom field is obj -> obj -> Sort 1, Subtype.{1} lands at Sort (max 1 1) = Sort 1, and Sigma.{u,v} lands at Sort (max u v + 1), one universe too high. The setoid cost of a bundled-hom category is ONE new proof (compCongr) plus three pointwise liftings of the object's own equiv laws; idL, idR and assoc are free.
